ca_bay_view_boulder.blurb: Bay View Boulder is a single sandstone boulder on Mount Tamalpais, in the Mount Tam bouldering zone of the Bay Area. It holds eight problems, ranging from V3 up to V12, with most of them in the V5 to V6 band, so it suits climbers who already boulder hard rather than beginners. The block faces southeast, which leaves it in shade through the afternoon, and the setting looks out toward San Francisco and the Pacific. Parking is right beside the rock, so there is almost no walk. Bring pads for a small circuit of problems that can fill a short session.

ca_prowe_area_the.blurb: The Prowe Area is one of the small sections of the Dixon Lake crags in northern San Diego County, centred on a large granite boulder reached by a short scramble above the neighbouring Y Crack section. It has eight lines: three on trad gear, three set up for top-roping, and two aid lines. Free climbs run from about 5.7 to 5.11, with a cluster around 5.10 and 5.11, so it leans toward intermediate and harder climbers. The routes here are short. It is reached from the main trail that heads toward the summit.

ca_ranger_station_rock_3.blurb: Ranger Station Rock 3 is a small tonalite boulder in Long Valley, in the San Jacinto Mountains, a very short walk west of the ranger station. It faces east and has eight problems, from VB up to V4, most of them in the easier half of that range, which makes it a good first or last stop of the day. The stone is of excellent quality, the landings are good and the top can be walked off. Because it sits so close to the start of the trail and has quite a few lines for its size, it can draw a crowd.

ca_raspberry_wall.blurb: Raspberry Wall is a continuous stretch of clean rock in upper Scheelite Canyon, one of the side canyons of Pine Creek near Bishop. It has eight routes, seven of them sport and one trad, nearly all at 5.11 with one 5.12 and one 5.13, so it is a place for strong climbers. The granodiorite is compact, and the climbing leans on slopers, slabs, mantles, roofs and stemming corners, where friction matters on the cruxes. Getting here means a steeper walk beyond the lower-canyon walls, which keeps it away from the larger crowds of the lower canyon.

ca_rich_and_famous_cliff.blurb: Rich And Famous Cliff is a short monzogranite formation in Joshua Tree, standing in front of the Big Hunk northeast face. It faces northeast, so it stays shaded and is a handy choice when the day is hot. There are eight routes, five trad, two sport and one top-rope, all between 5.8 and 5.10, with most at 5.9 and 5.10. The trad lines are moderate cracks, and a few newer face climbs have been added. It is a straightforward stop for climbers working through the middle grades, reached from the main Echo Tee parking area by the same walk used for the neighbouring wall.

ca_reef_rock.blurb: Reef Rock is one of the formations in the Towers of Uncertainty group in Joshua Tree, found by walking west from Crow's Nest. Its face is crossed by several horizontal cracks, and the monzogranite is compact and in good shape. There are eight routes, seven trad and one top-rope, from about 5.7 to 5.10, with half of them at 5.10, so the mix suits climbers comfortable on crack and face moves in the middle grades. The group is reached from a pullout on Geology Tour Road followed by a short walk.

ca_scot_rock_west_face.blurb: This wall is the lower of the two faces of Scot Rock, near Lake Arrowhead on the southern edge of the San Bernardino Mountains. It stands about 80 feet tall and carries eight routes, five trad and three sport, mostly from 5.7 to 5.9, plus one very easy line, so it is friendly to newer leaders and groups of mixed ability. The rock is high quality, and the lines mix crack, face and slab climbing. Climbers get to the base by rappelling in, or by scrambling down steep but easy ground beside the routes.

ca_sector_f.blurb: Sector F is a wall of boulder problems in the Ravine, a small bouldering area near Mammoth Lakes. It has eight problems, mostly V0 and V1 with one V3, so it works well for warming up or for newer boulderers. The wall is on the left side of the ravine, roughly 300 yards up from the start, and can be recognised by a large, chalked incut hold that starts a dyno problem. The stone is good, and the area as a whole gets heavy winter snow, which makes it a warm-weather venue.
